is connected in series with resistors of resistances 5.00 Ω, 10.0 Ω and 15.0 Ω.

The potential difference (p.d.) between P and Q is balanced against 12.5 cm of the resistance
wire, so that the ammeter reads zero.
The p.d. across the other resistors is then balanced against other lengths of the resistance wire.
Which balanced lengths of resistance wire correspond to the connection points given in the

hints: Notice that P to Q is only the $5.00 \, \Omega$ resistor and it balances $12.5 \, \text{cm}$ of the uniform $100 \, \text{cm}$ wire XY.
Connect the two proportionalities: in the M loop the same current gives $V = IR$ so $V$ is proportional to $R$, and on uniform wire XY $V$ is proportional to balance length.

Compare each new resistance to $5.00 \, \Omega$: $10.0 \, \Omega$ is $2$ times, $10.0+15.0 \, \Omega$ is $5$ times, and $5.00+10.0 \, \Omega$ is $3$ times, then multiply $12.5 \, \text{cm}$ by each factor.
walkthrough: Identify the calibration: $V_{PQ}$ across $5.00 \, \Omega$ balances $l_{PQ} = 12.5 \, \text{cm}$ with zero ammeter current, so no current is drawn from the test circuit at balance.

State the physics: resistors P-Q-R-S are in series with cell M, so current $I$ is common and $V = IR$ gives $V$ proportional to $R$. The wire XY is uniform, so balance p.d. is proportional to balance length $l$. Hence $l$ is proportional to $R$.
For Q and R the resistance is $10.0 \, \Omega$, which is $10.0/5.00 = 2$ times $R_{PQ}$. So $l = 2 \times 12.5 \, \text{cm} = 25.0 \, \text{cm}$.
For Q and S the resistance is $10.0 + 15.0 = 25.0 \, \Omega$, which is $25.0/5.00 = 5$ times $R_{PQ}$. So $l = 5 \times 12.5 \, \text{cm} = 62.5 \, \text{cm}$.
For P and R the resistance is $5.00 + 10.0 = 15.0 \, \Omega$, which is $15.0/5.00 = 3$ times $R_{PQ}$. So $l = 3 \times 12.5 \, \text{cm} = 37.5 \, \text{cm}$.
The set $25.0 \, \text{cm}$, $62.5 \, \text{cm}$, $37.5 \, \text{cm}$ matches the table column for Q-R, Q-S, P-R. This is option B.

A.explanation: Q and R across $10.0 \, \Omega$ cannot balance the same $12.5 \, \text{cm}$ as P and Q across $5.00 \, \Omega$ because p.d. is proportional to resistance.

B.explanation: Lengths scale with resistance from the $5.00 \, \Omega$ to $12.5 \, \text{cm}$ base, giving $25.0 \, \text{cm}$, $62.5 \, \text{cm}$ and $37.5 \, \text{cm}$.

C.explanation: Q and S across $25.0 \, \Omega$ is $5$ times the $5.00 \, \Omega$ p.d., so $5 \times 12.5 = 62.5 \, \text{cm}$, not $75.0 \, \text{cm}$.

D.explanation: P and R across $15.0 \, \Omega$ is $3$ times the P-Q p.d., so $3 \times 12.5 = 37.5 \, \text{cm}$, not $12.5 \, \text{cm}$.
